text:
elyse: Heads-up — noticed a weird early cut in streaming for a new HF->Redwood conversion. The model has two special EOS tokens and the stream sometimes terminates after the first partial token appears in a frame.

ravi: @elyse can you paste a minimal repro (tokenizer config + stream frames)? curious if it's tokenization vs stop-seq matching. :thinking_face: 

elyse: minimal snippets below. model config has `</s>` and `<EOS_ALT>` as separate special tokens. tokenizer.json shows `<EOS_ALT>` tokenized as two ids in the bytepair vocab. Streaming frames look like this: 

```
frame 1: "... The result was surpri"
frame 2: "sed </"  
frame 3: "s>\n"
```

When we feed frames into the stop matcher, frame 2 contains `"</"` which corresponds to token id 4021 (a standalone token in this vocab) and the matcher flags an EOS prematurely.

micah: That sounds like a token boundary/multi-token stop mismatch rather than Redwood's stream logic. HF tokenizers sometimes split special tokens into multiple ids depending on training. If your stop matcher treats sequences of token ids as text substrings it can hit false positives when the stream is chunked arbitrarily.

elyse: Example config snippet: 
```json
{
  "special_tokens": {
    "eos_token": "</s>",
    "additional_special_tokens": ["<EOS_ALT>"]
  }
}
```
And tokenizer mapping (simplified): 
```
"<EOS_ALT>": [4021, 98]
"</s>": [2]
```

ravi: If `<EOS_ALT>` maps to multiple ids we need to ensure the streaming stop detector buffers token id history across frames and only matches full multi-id sequences, not partial. Is our tokenizer->detokenizer mapping preserved during conversion?

elyse: Looks like we preserved text-level special tokens in config.json but conversion left the internal id mapping to the runtime tokenizer (we rely on HF tokenizers at conversion time). The HF tokenizer sometimes represents `<EOS_ALT>` as `</` + `s>` token pieces depending on merge rules, so the runtime saw `</` as a standalone token id 4021 and matched it against a naive stop pattern of `"</s>"` as substring.

micah: Two actionable fixes: 1) make the stop matcher operate on token id sequences instead of raw string substrings for special tokens that are registered in the tokenizer; 2) during conversion, canonicalize special tokens to the tokenizer's token ids and store them as id arrays in the model metadata. The second avoids text-level substring matching bugs.

elyse: Confirmed #1 works locally: switched stop detection to token-id suffix matching with a small rolling buffer and now streaming doesn't cut on the partial token. Patch attached to branch `ml/eos-token-buffer`. Short diff: 
```diff
- if text.endswith(stop_str): end_stream()
+ if token_buffer.ends_with(stop_token_ids): end_stream()
```

ravi: Nice. Can we add a conversion-time validation that checks each special token's id sequence length and emits a warning if length > 1? That would catch models where special tokens are multi-id.

micah: Agree. Also add an integration test for streaming where we artificially chunk outputs at arbitrary byte boundaries to ensure no early termination.

eng-bot: CI pipeline triggered: ml/eos-token-buffer -> unit tests + streaming-integration (queued).

elyse: I'll open the PR and include a small reproducer and notes about HF tokenizer quirks + suggested release note. FYI tagging eng-sre for visibility in case any dedicated runtime nodes rely on older matching logic.

ravi: Thanks. Also link to HF tokenizers doc for reference: https://huggingface.co/docs/tokenizers/overview

micah: One more gotcha — some evals expect trailing `</s>` to be stripped; ensure post-processing still behaves the same when switching to id-based stops. Might need to keep the canonical text-level mapping in the response pipeline for downstream eval comparators.

elyse: Good call. I'll add an integration check in the eval harness to compare text-trimmed vs id-trimmed outputs across the regression suite.

ravi: Sounds good. Keep us posted and ping if you want a quick review. :+1:
